evidence.text: Edward attended clinic accompanied by his daughter. He has an established diagnosis of focal epilepsy following an ischemic stroke three years ago.

He describes recurring focal motor seizures involving clonic jerking of the right hand. His most recent event occurred sometime around Christmas, though the exact calendar date was not noted by the family. He had a prior focal attack a few months ago in autumn 2024. He reports no other seizure patterns or convulsions. He continues levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily.
I requested a routine outpatient EEG today to reassess his baseline epileptiform activity. It has not yet been performed. Follow-up in five months.
I reviewed Edward in clinic today. His diagnosis remains post-stroke focal epilepsy.

The routine outpatient EEG requested on 1 February was performed in late March. Its report became available to our clinical team in early April and demonstrated left frontotemporal sharp waves consistent with his focal lesion. He experienced another focal motor attack sometime in late spring, probably May 2025. He reports no other seizure types.
He continues levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily without change. Next review in autumn.
Edward attended for routine review. He reports continuing stability on levetiracetam, with his last focal motor seizure occurring over the summer.
No changes made. Routine follow-up next year.
